newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Leftists launch series of protests against APEC.
newsitem.headline: Leftists launch series of protests against APEC.

text.p: Hundreds of leftist activists on Thursday began a series of protests against plans to create the world's biggest free trade region.

Leaders announced that thousands of Filipinos eventually would take part in a series of demonstrations and strikes over the next four days to protest against the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Subic Bay on Monday which will be attended by U.S. President Bill Clinton and other world leaders.
If their plans are realised it will be the biggest display of popular discontent with APEC's since the grouping was conceived in 1989 to nurture the economic growth of the Pacific Rim.
Objectors say the organisation amounts to little more than a club to help big business exploit the underprivileged.

As foreign and economic ministers representing 18 economies flew into the Philippines to prepare for Monday's summit, more than 1,000 demonstrators, with a handful of Roman Catholic priests in the forefront, gathered to march through Manila towards the presidential palace.
Riot police stopped the demonstrators, some of whom wore Clinton and President Ferdinand Ramos masks, after they had gone only a few metres (feet). Police said they needed a permit.
Across town more than 200 delegates from 34 countries began a three-day meeting in a suburban hotel to object to what they said was the false progress of the rich capitalist nations.
Peasant leaders from Mexico, trade unionists from Canada and a group of Filipina nuns denounced APEC for creating poverty and unemployment and destroying the fabric of native communities.
"Our call here is 'junk APEC'," said Satur Ocampo, spokesman for the People's Conference Against Imperialist Globalisation.

Nathaniel Santiago, secretary-general of the leftist labour alliance Bagong Alyansang Makabayan, said delegates would join a motorcade of 20,000 people from Manila to Subic on Sunday to protest against the summit at the former U.S. naval base.
He predicted some 200,000 people would join in nationwide protests on Saturday and in transport and other industrial strikes on the day of the summit.

Nanjundo Swamy, a leader of an Indian peasants' organisation, said the United States was attempting through APEC and the World Trade Oreganisation (WTO) to do what Christopher Columbus had begun in the 15th century -- conquering undeveloped lands for exploitation by the rich.
"Globalisation is nothiung but the rebirth of Christopher Columbus," he said.
APEC's 18 members are committed to removing trade barriers by the year 2020, embracing half of the people on earth in the world's largest free trade bloc.
Speakers at the conference said globalisation threatened jobs because it removed protective tariff barriers which allowed small farmers and others in the Third World to survive.
It also threatened liberal social programmes as it forced Third World countries to reduce spending on health care, unemployment insurance and other benefits.
